title: People
goal: Say what someone is like and what they look like, point people out in a crowd, talk about friends, partners and in-laws, and pass on (or refuse to pass on) a bit of gossip.
intro:
Half of all conversation is about other people: the new guy at work, a friend's boyfriend, your sister's in-laws. This unit gives you words for character (मिलनसार 'easy-going', कञ्जुस 'stingy', रिसाहा 'short-tempered'), looks and relationships — including the English words young Nepalis really use, like **गर्लफ्रेन्ड** and **लभ म्यारेज**.

The grammar is the full **relative clause**. Nepali has no 'who' or 'that' in everyday speech: the description comes *before* the person, built on a participle — **चस्मा लगाएको** केटा 'the guy (who is) wearing glasses', **हिजो भेटेकी** केटी 'the girl (who) we met yesterday'. You'll also learn to say how people **seem**: थाकेको **जस्तो देखिन्छ** 'he looks tired', घमण्डी **जस्तो लाग्यो** 'he struck me as arrogant'.

grammar.title: Relative clauses in full: the description comes first
grammar.body:
English puts 'who/that' clauses **after** the noun: 'the guy *who is wearing glasses*'. Everyday Nepali puts the description **before** the noun, using a participle, with no word for 'who':

**-एको** (done, or a state): **चस्मा लगाएको** केटा 'the guy wearing glasses' · **हिजो आएको** मान्छे 'the man who came yesterday'
**-ने** (habitual, general or future): **नेपाली बोल्ने** विदेशी 'foreigners who speak Nepali' · **सँगै काम गर्ने** साथी 'a friend I work with'

The clause keeps its own subject, with **ले** where the past needs it: **मैले भेटेको** केटा 'the guy I met' · **दिदीले बनाएको** खाना 'the food my sister made'.

**Agreement**: -एको changes like an adjective — **-एको** (masc.), **-एकी** (fem.), **-एका** (plural or respectful): लगाए**की** केटी, आए**का** पाहुनाहरू. In fast speech many people use -एको for everyone, but -एकी sounds right. -ने never changes.

**Negative**: add **न-**: **नआएका** साथीहरू 'the friends who didn't come', **नबोल्ने** मान्छे 'someone who doesn't talk'.

**'With' a feature** uses **भएको** 'having': **दाह्री भएको** मान्छे 'the man with a beard', **लामो कपाल भएकी** केटी 'the girl with long hair'.

**'The type who'**: **-ने खालको**: ऊ झगडा गर्**ने खालको** होइन 'he's not the type to pick fights'.

The participle can also stand alone as a noun: **मैले भनेको** 'what I said', **चस्मा लगाउने** 'the one with glasses'. The correlative जो…ऊ / जुन…त्यो pattern from unit 20 is for careful speech and long clauses.

grammar.title: Seems, looks like: देखिन्छ, जस्तो, लाग्छ
grammar.body:
**देखिनु** 'to look, appear' + an adjective describes what you see: ऊ खुसी **देखिन्छ** 'he looks happy'. It conjugates normally: म देखिन्छु · तिमी **देखिन्छौ** · ऊ देखिन्छ · उनी **देखिन्छिन्** (f) · उनीहरू देखिन्छन् · तपाईं **देखिनुहुन्छ**.

**जस्तो** 'like' and **जस्तै** 'just like' follow a noun, joined: बुबा**जस्तै** देखिन्छ 'looks just like his dad', हिरो**जस्तो** 'like a film star'.

**As if**: participle + **जस्तो**: ऊ थाकेको **जस्तो** देखिन्छ 'he looks (as if he's) tired', ऊ भर्खर उठेको जस्तो छ 'he looks like he's just got up'. With -ने it's 'looks like it's going to' (unit 13): पानी पर्ने जस्तो छ.

**Seems to me**: **मलाई** X **जस्तो लाग्छ / लाग्यो** — an impression rather than a look: मलाई ऊ अलि घमण्डी जस्तो लाग्यो 'he struck me as a bit arrogant'.

**Turns out**: when the first impression was wrong, Nepali reaches for **रहेछ** (unit 20): पहिले घमण्डी जस्तो लागेको थियो, तर ऊ त सोझो **रहेछ** 'at first he seemed arrogant, but he turns out to be a sweet, simple guy'.

**The trap**: after a verb, जस्तो needs the participle, not the past: **थाकेको जस्तो**, never थाक्यो जस्तो. And देखिन्छ is about appearance, लाग्छ about your impression.

examples.en: You look younger than your age.
He looks like he's just got up.
You look just like a film star in this photo!

dialogue.title: Who was that guy?
dialogue.setting: Sarah and Bibek over coffee in Jhamsikhel, the morning after a friend's birthday party. Their friend Anjali is due to join them.

lines.en: Tall, with glasses? His name's Rohan. Anjali's boyfriend, apparently!

lines.roman: tin mahinā bhayo re. tara kasailāi nabhannu hai, Añjalile malāi mātra bhaneki ho.
lines.en: Three months, apparently. But don't tell anyone, OK — Anjali only told me.

lines.speaker: Sarah

lines.speaker: Bibek

lines.roman: pahile ta ali ghamanḍi jasto lāgeko thiyo, tara kurā gardā ekdam milansār rahechha.

lines.speaker: Sarah

lines.native: इन्जिनियर रे। अनि अञ्जलीकी आमासँग पनि राम्रै मिल्छ रे।

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: ओहो! त्यसो भए त बिहे पनि छिट्टै होला!
lines.roman: oho! tyaso bhae ta bihe pani chhiṭṭai holā!
lines.en: Ooh! Then there'll be a wedding soon!

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: तिमी पनि न! अरूको कुरा काट्न कति मज्जा लाग्छ तिमीलाई!
lines.roman: timi pani na! aruko kurā kāṭna kati majjā lāgchha timilāi!
lines.en: Oh, you! You really love gossiping, don't you!

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: मैले के गरेँ? तिमीले नै सुरु गरेको हो नि!
lines.roman: maile ke gareṃ? timile nai suru gareko ho ni!
lines.en: What did I do? You're the one who started it!

lines.speaker: Bibek
lines.native: ल ल, चुप! अञ्जली आइन्, उता हेर।
lines.roman: la la, chup! Añjali āin, utā hera.
lines.en: OK, OK — shh! Anjali's here, look over there.

culture:
Nepalis comment on looks far more directly than English speakers: **मोटाउनुभयो** 'you've put on weight' or **दुब्लाउनुभयो** 'you've got thin' are ordinary, even friendly, remarks from relatives. Questions about marriage are normal too — **बिहे भयो?**, and then **लभ कि मागी?** 'love or arranged?'. Love marriages are now common in cities, but most families still expect to be involved.

Family vocabulary is richer than English: there are separate words for your older sister's husband (**भिनाजु**) and younger sister's husband (**ज्वाइँ**), and in-laws are addressed by kinship terms, never by name. The **सासू–बुहारी** (mother-in-law vs daughter-in-law) tension is a staple of jokes and TV serials.

When gossiping, keep the respect levels: someone older is still **उहाँ** even behind their back, and dropping to **ऊ** for an elder sounds disrespectful. Young people mix in English freely — गर्लफ्रेन्ड, ब्वाइफ्रेन्ड, क्रस 'crush', ब्रेकअप — while **कुरा काट्नु** 'to gossip' is the word for what everyone claims not to do.

tip.title: Describing people: हो or छ?
tip.body:
- Adjective alone → **छ**: ऊ मेहनती **छ**, उनी दयालु **छिन्**, दाइ मेहनती **हुनुहुन्छ**.
- Adjective + **मान्छे** (a noun) → **हो**: ऊ मिलनसार केटा **हो**.
- Character: **X स्वभावको**: राम्रो स्वभावको मान्छे.
tip.pattern: ऊ + adj + छ  ·  ऊ + adj + मान्छे + हो

lessons.title: Not so nice: lazy, stingy, stuck-up

tip.title: The type who…: -ने खालको
tip.body:
- **verb-ने खालको** = 'the kind of person who…': चाँडो **नउठ्ने खालको** 'not the type to get up early'.
- Negative: **न** + verb-ने: **नबोल्ने**, **नतिर्ने**.
- -ने before a noun = 'who (does)': चुरोट **खाने** मान्छे 'people who smoke'.
- -ओ adjectives turn to **-ई** for women: बाठो → **बाठी**, सोझो → सोझी.

lessons.title: Pointing people out

tip.title: The guy wearing…, the girl with…
tip.body:
- Description **before** the person, no 'who': चस्मा **लगाएको** केटा.
- **-एको** (m) · **-एकी** (f) · **-एका** (pl.): लगाए**की** केटी, आए**का** मान्छेहरू.
- 'With' a feature: **भएको**: दाह्री **भएको** मान्छे.
- Its own doer takes ले: **मैले भनेको** मान्छे 'the guy I told you about'.

sentences.roman: saṃgai kām garne sāthiharu sabai ramāilā chhan.
sentences.en: The people I work with are all fun.

sentences.native: नयाँ आएका मान्छेहरू कहाँबाट हुन्?
sentences.roman: nayāṃ āekā mānchheharu kahāṃbāṭa hun?
sentences.en: Where are the new people from?

lessons.title: You look tired! He seems nice

tip.title: Looks like, seems: देखिन्छ, जस्तो, लाग्छ
tip.body:
- **देखिनु** 'look': तिमी खुसी **देखिन्छौ**, उनी **देखिन्छिन्**.
- Noun + **जस्तै** 'just like': आमा**जस्तै**.
- Participle + **जस्तो** 'as if': थाकेको **जस्तो** देखिन्छ (not थाक्यो जस्तो).
- Impression: मलाई ऊ घमण्डी जस्तो **लाग्यो**. Wrong impression? → ऊ त सोझो **रहेछ**!

sentences.native: तिमी आज खुसी देखिन्छौ, के भयो?
sentences.roman: timi āja khusi dekhinchhau, ke bhayo?
sentences.en: You look happy today — what's up?

sentences.native: उनी आमाजस्तै देखिन्छिन्।
sentences.roman: uni āmājastai dekhinchhin.
sentences.en: She looks just like her mum.

sentences.native: ऊ दिक्क लागेको जस्तो देखिन्छ।
sentences.roman: u dikka lāgeko jasto dekhinchha.
sentences.en: He looks fed up.

sentences.native: मलाई ऊ अलि घमण्डी जस्तो लाग्यो।
sentences.roman: malāi u ali ghamanḍi jasto lāgyo.
sentences.en: He struck me as a bit arrogant.

sentences.native: पहिलो पटक भेट्दा ऊ लजालु जस्तो लाग्यो।
sentences.roman: pahilo paṭak bheṭdā u lajālu jasto lāgyo.
sentences.en: When I first met him he seemed shy.

sentences.native: ऊ त धेरै मिलनसार रहेछ!
sentences.roman: u ta dherai milansār rahechha!
sentences.en: Turns out he's really easy-going!

sentences.native: यो खाना त आमाले बनाएको जस्तै छ!
sentences.roman: yo khānā ta āmāle banāeko jastai chha!
sentences.en: This food is just like Mum makes!

sentences.native: हाम्रो चिनजान एउटा पार्टीमा भएको थियो।
sentences.roman: hāmro chinjān euṭā pārṭimā bhaeko thiyo.
sentences.en: We got to know each other at a party.

sentences.native: तिमी बिरामी जस्तो देखिन्छौ, ठीक छौ?
sentences.roman: timi birāmi jasto dekhinchhau, ṭhik chhau?
sentences.en: You look ill — are you OK?

sentences.native: हेर्दा त ऊ बीस वर्षको जस्तो देखिन्छ!
sentences.roman: herdā ta u bis barsako jasto dekhinchha!
sentences.en: To look at him you'd think he was twenty!

sentences.native: उहाँ मेरो पुरानो चिनजानको मान्छे हुनुहुन्छ।
sentences.roman: uhāṃ mero purāno chinjānko mānchhe hunuhunchha.
sentences.en: He's an old acquaintance of mine.

sentences.native: म र दाइ धेरै मिल्छौँ।
sentences.roman: ma ra dāi dherai milchhauṃ.
sentences.en: My brother and I get on really well.

sentences.native: ऊ मसँग मिल्दैन।
sentences.roman: u masaṃga mildaina.
sentences.en: He and I don't get on.

sentences.native: तिम्रो ब्वाइफ्रेन्ड के गर्छ?
sentences.roman: timro bwāiphrenḍ ke garchha?
sentences.en: What does your boyfriend do?

sentences.native: उसको गर्लफ्रेन्ड पोखराकी हो।
sentences.roman: usko garlphrenḍ pokharāki ho.
sentences.en: His girlfriend is from Pokhara.

sentences.native: उनीहरूको सम्बन्ध कति वर्ष भयो?
sentences.roman: uniharuko sambandha kati barsa bhayo?
sentences.en: How many years have they been together?

sentences.native: उनीहरू सँगै राम्रा देखिन्छन्।
sentences.roman: uniharu saṃgai rāmrā dekhinchhan.
sentences.en: They look good together.

sentences.native: हाम्रो बिहे मागी हो, तर हामी धेरै मिल्छौँ।
sentences.roman: hāmro bihe māgi ho, tara hāmi dherai milchhauṃ.
sentences.en: Ours was an arranged marriage, but we get on really well.

sentences.native: तिमीहरू कसरी भेट्यौ?
sentences.roman: timiharu kasari bheṭyau?
sentences.en: How did you two meet?

sentences.native: मेरो सबैभन्दा मिल्ने साथी काठमाडौंमा बस्छ।
sentences.roman: mero sabaibhandā milne sāthi kāṭhmāḍauṃmā baschha.
sentences.en: My best friend lives in Kathmandu.

sentences.native: तिमी उसको परिवारसँग मिल्छौ?
sentences.roman: timi usko pariwārsaṃga milchhau?
sentences.en: Do you get on with his family?

sentences.native: सुरुमा हामी मिल्दैनथ्यौँ, अहिले मिल्ने साथी भयौँ।
sentences.roman: surumā hāmi mildainathyauṃ, ahile milne sāthi bhayauṃ.
sentences.en: At first we didn't get on — now we're close friends.

lessons.title: Family drama and a bit of gossip

tip.title: Gossip grammar: रे and रहेछ
tip.body:
- **रे** at the end = 'apparently, so I hear': झगडा भयो **रे**.
- **रहेछ** = 'turns out' — you've just found out yourself: ऊ त बाठो पो **रहेछ**!
- Habit you've discovered: verb-**दो रहेछ**: हाम्रो कुरा काट्**दो रहेछ** 'turns out he gossips about us'.

sentences.native: सासू र बुहारीको झगडा सधैँ हुन्छ रे।
sentences.roman: sāsu ra buhāriko jhagaḍā sadhaiṃ hunchha re.
sentences.en: Apparently the mother-in-law and the daughter-in-law are always fighting.

sentences.native: मेरो भिनाजु त धेरै रमाइलो मान्छे रहेछ।
sentences.roman: mero bhināju ta dherai ramāilo mānchhe rahechha.
sentences.en: My brother-in-law turns out to be a really fun guy.

sentences.native: दिदी र भिनाजु अर्को महिना अमेरिका जाँदै हुनुहुन्छ रे।
sentences.roman: didi ra bhināju arko mahinā Amerikā jāṃdai hunuhunchha re.
sentences.en: Apparently my sister and her husband are moving to America next month.

sentences.native: हाम्रो नयाँ ज्वाइँ डाक्टर हुनुहुन्छ रे।
sentences.roman: hāmro nayāṃ jwāiṃ ḍākṭar hunuhunchha re.
sentences.en: Apparently our new son-in-law is a doctor.

sentences.native: नयाँ बुहारी कस्ती छिन्?
sentences.roman: nayāṃ buhāri kasti chhin?
sentences.en: What's the new daughter-in-law like?

sentences.native: अरूको कुरा काट्नु राम्रो होइन।
sentences.roman: aruko kurā kāṭnu rāmro hoina.
sentences.en: It's not nice to gossip about other people.

sentences.native: बुहारीले सासूलाई केही भनिन् रे, अनि झगडा भयो।
sentences.roman: buhārile sāsulāi kehi bhanin re, ani jhagaḍā bhayo.
sentences.en: Apparently the daughter-in-law said something to her mother-in-law, and then there was a fight.

sentences.native: उनीहरूको बिहे भयो रे, थाहा छ?
sentences.roman: uniharuko bihe bhayo re, thāhā chha?
sentences.en: They got married, apparently — did you know?

sentences.native: मलाई त ऊ सोझो जस्तो लागेको थियो, तर बाठो पो रहेछ!
sentences.roman: malāi ta u sojho jasto lāgeko thiyo, tara bāṭho po rahechha!
sentences.en: I thought he was naive, but turns out he's quite the operator!

sentences.native: के कुरा काटिरहेका छौ? मलाई पनि भन न!
sentences.roman: ke kurā kāṭirahekā chhau? malāi pani bhana na!
sentences.en: What are you two gossiping about? Tell me too!

sentences.native: भिनाजुले फेरि जागिर छोड्नुभयो रे।
sentences.roman: bhinājule pheri jāgir chhoḍnubhayo re.
sentences.en: Apparently my brother-in-law has quit his job again.

sentences.native: ऊ त हाम्रो कुरा काट्दो रहेछ!
sentences.roman: u ta hāmro kurā kāṭdo rahechha!
sentences.en: Turns out he gossips about us!
